presentation.summary: Submit Silo movie and series requests through a Seerr-compatible server.
presentation.description_markdown: Connects Silo to Seerr, including Jellyseerr and Overseerr-compatible deployments. Seerr continues to manage its own Sonarr and Radarr services. The plugin sends each title as one Seerr request, with the server, quality profile and root folder you choose, and maps Silo request identities and request status.
presentation.setup_markdown: Install the plugin and add a Seerr connection in Silo with its base URL and an API key owned by a Seerr administrator. Choose whether requests should be attributed to the API-key owner or mapped to Silo users by email. Optionally, pick the Radarr and Sonarr server, quality profile and root folder that requests get; Silo request routes can override them per rule. The quality profile decides the resolution, so one Radarr or Sonarr can serve both HD and 4K. To spread requests over several disks, turn on storage groups: named lists of root folders that are filled in order or by free space, with the next group taking over when one is full.

capabilities.description: Fulfill content requests through a Seerr (Overseerr/Jellyseerr) instance.

fields.label: Attribute requests to
fields.description: Admin user: all requests come from the API-key owner (auto-approved). Map to Silo users: attribute each request to the Seerr user matching the requester's email (created if missing).

fields.label: Auto-approve requests
fields.description: Mapped users' requests are auto-approved. Off: they land in Seerr's per-user approval queue.

fields.label: Fail the request if the user can't be mapped
fields.description: On: a request whose Silo user can't be matched/created on Seerr fails instead of being submitted under the admin.

fields.label: Use storage groups
fields.description: On: the plugin chooses each request's root folder from the storage groups below, by free space, and the root folder settings under Movies and Series are replaced by a storage group setting. Off: requests use the root folder settings.

fields.label: Minimum free space (GB)
fields.description: A folder with less free space than this counts as full and is skipped. When every folder of a group is full, the next group is used. When all groups are full, the request fails with a message.

fields.label: Name
fields.description: Shown where the group can be picked: in the storage group settings and in Silo's routing rules. A pick is stored by this name, so renaming a group means picking it again there. Without a name it is called Group and its number.

fields.label: Radarr folders (movies)
fields.description: The Radarr root folders in this group, kept in the order you select them. They are the folders of the Radarr server chosen under Movies; test the connection to load them. Leave empty if this group holds no movies.

fields.label: Sonarr folders (series)
fields.description: The Sonarr root folders in this group, kept in the order you select them. They are the folders of the Sonarr server chosen under Series; test the connection to load them. Leave empty if this group holds no series.

fields.label: Choose a folder
fields.description: In order: fill the first folder until it is full, then the next. Most free space: each request goes to the folder with the most free space, which spreads requests over the folders.

fields.label: Radarr server (movies)
fields.description: The Seerr Radarr server that movie requests go to. Ignored for series. Seerr default uses the server Seerr marks as default. Servers Seerr marks as 4K are not listed. Silo request routes can override this per rule.

fields.label: Radarr quality profile (movies)
fields.description: The quality profile movie requests get on that Radarr server. It decides the resolution: pick a profile that allows 4K to get 4K. Seerr default uses the profile set for the server in Seerr. After changing the server, test the connection to load its profiles. Silo request routes can override this per rule.

fields.label: Movie quality profile is chosen by
fields.description: Who picks the quality profile of a movie request. Admin: always the quality profile above. Requester: the person requesting picks one, and an admin can change it when approving. Admin on approval: the admin picks one when approving. The quality profile above stays the preselected value, and applies when nobody picks, such as for requests approved automatically. Needs a Silo server that supports request options.

fields.label: Radarr root folder (movies)
fields.description: The folder movie requests are saved to on that Radarr server. Seerr default uses the folder set for the server in Seerr. Silo request routes can override this per rule.

fields.label: Storage group (movies)
fields.description: Storage groups are on, so they choose the root folder of a movie request. Automatic starts at the first group. Pick a group to start there instead; when it is full, the groups after it follow. If no group has Radarr folders, Seerr's default folder is used. After changing the groups, test the connection to refresh this list. Silo request routes can override this per rule.

fields.label: Movie root folder is chosen by
fields.description: Who picks the root folder of a movie request. Admin: always the root folder above. Requester: the person requesting picks one, and an admin can change it when approving. Admin on approval: the admin picks one when approving. Requesters then see the folder paths. The root folder above stays the preselected value, and applies when nobody picks, such as for requests approved automatically. Needs a Silo server that supports request options.

fields.label: Sonarr server (series)
fields.description: The Seerr Sonarr server that series requests go to. Ignored for movies. Seerr default uses the server Seerr marks as default. Servers Seerr marks as 4K are not listed. Silo request routes can override this per rule.

fields.label: Sonarr quality profile (series)
fields.description: The quality profile series requests get on that Sonarr server, anime included. It decides the resolution: pick a profile that allows 4K to get 4K. Seerr default uses the profile set for the server in Seerr. After changing the server, test the connection to load its profiles. Silo request routes can override this per rule.

Needs a Silo server that supports request options.

fields.label: Sonarr root folder (series)

fields.description: Storage groups are on, so they choose the root folder of a series request. Automatic starts at the first group. Pick a group to start there instead; when it is full, the groups after it follow. If no group has Sonarr folders, Seerr's default folder is used.
